inputs: All 65,536 blocks of a 16-bit toy Feistel network, 4 rounds, non-injective F(x,k)=(x+k) mod 4
expected: Every block decrypts back to its original value with reversed keys
limitations: A finite toy network; it demonstrates structural invertibility, not the security of any real cipher.

inputs: The 8-bit function F(x,k)=(x+k) mod 4 over all 256 inputs for a fixed key
expected: Each of the four outputs has 64 preimages; the network still round-trips on all 65,536 blocks
limitations: Shows a deliberately non-invertible round function; it does not model a real cipher's F or key schedule.

inputs: The same 16-bit toy network with 3 and 4 rounds, all 65,536 blocks
expected: Both round counts round-trip on every block; invertibility does not distinguish 3 from 4 rounds
limitations: Round-trip correctness only; the Luby–Rackoff security distinction is a theoretical model result, not an executable attack test.

inputs: DES round/block parameters and the TDEA composition of three DES calls
expected: DES: 64-bit block, 32+32 halves, 16 rounds; TDEA: 3 x 16 = 48 rounds, block still 64 bits
limitations: Counting only; these are concrete algorithm parameters, not fixed properties of Feistel.
